cues.text: Dresses and skirts must be even all the way around. The secret is measuring from the floor.
The customer wears the shoes they will wear with the dress.
Agree on the length at the front first.
Then use a ruler or yardstick standing on the floor, and pin at the same height all the way around.
Ask the customer to turn slowly, a little at a time, while you stay in one place.
Pin every few inches. Pins go across the fold.
Let them look in the mirror, front and back.
Write the length on the ticket, like: hem two inches, measured from floor, with heels.
Leave these for the tailor: wedding and formal gowns, dresses with many layers, beading, lace or a train, and fitting straps or the top of a dress. Book a fitting time instead.
